summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted after experiencing hypotension and left-sided chest tightness during a hemodialysis session. She received fluid resuscitation in the emergency department, which improved her blood pressure and resolved symptoms. A chest X-ray showed no acute intrathoracic process. Blood cultures later identified coagulase-negative Staphylococcus, leading to a diagnosis of bacteremia, likely catheter-related. She was treated with vancomycin, and repeat cultures were negative. She completed a hemodialysis session during admission without complications. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with instructions to resume warfarin and antihypertensive medications with adjustments on dialysis days, continue dialysis four times weekly, monitor vital signs, and follow up for INR and infection clearance.
